key_decisions: PROMOTE IS A RELEASE GATE, NOT A SHIP STEP - the user challenged the previous handoff on this and was RIGHT. .claude/skills/mpi-release/SKILL.md Preconditions already makes the dev-vs-stable manifest comparison a release gate and says 'Never auto-promote - it is a live op affecting released users, same class as git push'. Independently, routes/remotePodLifecycle.js:147 POD_IMAGE_VERSION = 'v0.17.0' is a frozen constant INSIDE the shipped binary, so a new image TAG cannot reach a released user either; only an app release bumping that constant can. The ship-order rule (wrapper before image) is real but orders things WITHIN a release. SUBSTANTIVE REASON not to promote early: wrapper 0.2.41's premise is 'every node's Python dep is in the one curated set the image installs', which is true of the NEW image and false of v0.17.0 - promoting hands a 1.3.0 user a wrapper that deleted the _run_node_requirements_only self-heal on an image whose deps were never curated.

start.sh HAS A SECOND PIP PATH AND MPI-413 MISSED IT. start.sh (lines ~211-236) loops every VOLUME custom node at EVERY BOOT and runs pip install -r requirements.txt. aa81d65 never touched it, and the publish confirmed it (start.sh sha was byte-identical to what was already live). Of the 7 code-only volume packs exactly one ships a requirements.txt - VideoHelperSuite, declaring opencv-python - so on the NEW image the Dockerfile bakes opencv-contrib-python-headless and then start.sh installs opencv-python on top: two cv2 distributions, last-writer-wins, the exact bug this card exists to kill. The MPI-341 IMPORT FAILED grep would NOT catch it, because both builds import fine. Silent.

THE GUARD IS KEYED ON THE CURATED FILE'S PRESENCE, NOT A VERSION. `if [ -f /opt/python_deps.txt ]` skips the loop; the existing loop moved unchanged into the elif. The new Dockerfile already COPYs python_deps.txt to /opt/python_deps.txt, so its presence IS the marker. Pre-curated images (v0.17.0, v0.18.0-dev) lack it and run the loop exactly as before - which is why this start.sh stays safe to promote to stable independently of the image it boots on.

THE APP-SIDE WRAPPER_VERSION BUMP IS COSMETIC, NOT A GATE. The previous handoff implied it was needed for verification. It is not: bootstrap.sh:85 UNSETS CUBRIC_WRAPPER_VERSION whenever the R2 fetch succeeds, so the fetched wrapper self-reports through /health regardless of what the app injected at Pod create. The constant is only the fallback label for a baked-wrapper boot plus the doc pin.

THE RESIZE VIDEO FAILURE WAS NOT AN MPI-413 REGRESSION - proved, with a negative control, not argued. Pod /object_info showed 1822 node types and ZERO VHS_*; POST /remote/model-present said comfyui-videohelpersuite present:false while comfyui_ultimatesdupscale (also code-only, also volume) said present:true. The wrapper code MPI-413 deleted only ran requirements.txt against an ALREADY-EXTRACTED folder and never downloaded a node, and start.sh's loop only touches folders that exist - neither could remove a working VHS. Root cause is MPI-438.

MPI-438 OPTION A CHOSEN BY THE USER - ensure the code-only universal packs on EVERY connect, matching what the local engine already does at boot. Rejected: lazy per-graph install (needs a graph-to-pack map at dispatch and still stalls mid-generation).

MPI-438's TEST CAUGHT DEAD CODE. Four sabotages: dropping the _isImageResident filter, dropping VideoHelperSuite, and an id-less dep were all caught; removing the `id` stamp in getUniversalWorkflowDeps PASSED - because all 112 DEPS entries already self-identify (dep.id === its key, verified). The spread was dead code carrying a comment that misstated the data; both were deleted. The test was also rewritten to call the SHIPPED selection (_universalVolumeNodeDeps) instead of a local copy of the expression, which as first written would have passed while the real filter drifted.
